source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-8

procedures.title: Steering coupling: remove and install
steps: Unbolt and remove the instrument panel column mounting bracket.

With one person in the driver's seat and one at the engine compartment, raise the column just enough to pull the coupling off the steering gear; the person under the hood guides any column shift levers through the dash opening.
If the car must be left at this stage, set the column back in its mounted position and loosely refit the mounting bracket to hold it.
Take the coupling out of the car.
Installation: raise the column for clearance and loosely fit the coupling onto the steering gear shaft, keeping the column supported in its normal position whenever it is not being moved.
Slide the coupling into its installed position and fit the clamp bolt.
Fasten the coupling to the column's flanged end with washers and nuts, keeping the coupling adjustment shown in figure 16 in the manual.
Refit the instrument panel column mounting bracket, torqued to the spec at the rear of the manual.
Plug in the column harness and, if fitted, the back-up lamp/neutral safety switch connector.
Refit the seal, protective covers and trim cover or boot (see figure 14 in the manual); on the Corvette these covers go on from the engine compartment side.
notes: Caution: never let the column hang from the dash area once the bracket is off, or it will distort; keep it supported in its normal position.
Chevrolet/Chevelle-only automatic indicator pointer and lower cover steps are omitted.
